newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan carmakers hire new workers as demand rises.
newsitem.headline: Japan carmakers hire new workers as demand rises.

text.p: Several of Japan's big carmakers are hiring new workers, as brisk demand both at home and abroad is spurring them to boost production.

Mazda Motor Corp said on Wednesday it will resume hiring temporary workers in April for the first time in more than four years, in response to rising exports and robust domestic demand for its Demio subcompact recreational vehicles.

Mazda, owned 33.4 percent by Ford Motor Co, will hire 300 temporary production workers at its flagship plant in Hiroshima prefecture, western Japan. Mazda suspended the hiring of temporary workers in November 1992 due to poor sales.

Mazda is now selling 6,000 to 7,000 Demios a month, far above its monthly sales target of 4,000, a Mazda spokesman said. The company had a particularly good month in March, selling a total of 11,104 Demios, including 1,800 vehicles sold as Ford Festiva Miniwagons, he added.
Mazda launched the Demio in August of last year.
Mazda's vehicle exports have been rising on a year-on-year basis since last October, due mainly to good demand in Europe for its new 323 model, called the Familia in Japan, he said.
Other Japanese carmakers are boosting their workforces as well.

Honda Motor Co will increase its force of temporary production workers to 3,900 in April and May from 3,600 as of end-March, due to strong demand for its recreational vehicle series and rising motorcycle output, a Honda spokesman said on Wednesday.
Nissan Motor Co in early March started hiring up to 500 new temporary workers due to the production of new models and rising exports, a Nissan spokesman said.
Nissan's president Yoshikazu Hanawa said last December the company would launch eight new models in 1997.
Not all of Japan's leading carmakers are adding extra production workers, however.
Mitsubishi Motors now has 2,800 temporary workers, down from more than 3,000 in March, according to a spokesman.
Toyota Motor Corp had 3,000 temporary workers as of March 1, a spokeswoman said.
